question: Do unchanged native project-skill bundles increase observed test-first behavior on implicit software requests, and what happens to externally checked correctness and efficiency?
pair_order: baseline first in odd repetitions, candidate first in even repetitions; no automatic retry
primary_metric: observed_test_first_process: confirmed successes / all 12 scheduled trials in each condition; fail and unknown reported separately

process_rubric.pass: Trace shows task-relevant test creation/change, then meaningful assertion failure on intended public behavior, then first implementation edit, then success of the same behavior tests. No visible weakening/removal to get GREEN.
process_rubric.fail: Observed implementation edit before meaningful behavior RED, including implementation and tests together; or a complete trial visibly implements without the required observed sequence. Import, syntax, dependency and fixture errors do not count as RED.
process_rubric.unknown: Missing/incomplete/ambiguous evidence; timeout/environment failure; unverifiable write or test weakening order. Do not infer a pass from narration or final Git diff.
process_rubric.review: Two independent reviewers receive pseudonymous command/file-change trace copies; skill-read chatter, condition names and temp workspace paths masked. Full raw traces preserved; blinding may be inferred from workflow. Review disagreement recorded and unresolved cases unknown.
process_rubric.strict_automated_tdd: unknown: no independent intermediate runtime snapshots, so this is observed process only

secondary_metrics: External all-criteria outcome success / 12 scheduled, with fail/unknown
Per-task outcome and observed-process counts / 3 scheduled
Reported input/cached/output tokens and elapsed wall time; no currency inference
Actual known-path skill reads as lower bounds, not discovery F1/adherence
interpretation: A strictly positive lower bound supports a local observed-process improvement on these fixed tasks only. Correctness gains must be shown separately. No observed correctness regression is not a noninferiority proof. Report token/time tradeoffs equally.
decision_rule: Complete all 24 scheduled calls once; no optional stopping, failed-trial deletion, post-result prompt/checker edits, or favorable task additions. Preserve original zero-effect experiment unchanged. No universal score, population or statistical-significance claim: 4 task clusters are not 12 independent tasks.
limits: Existing host authentication/global/managed policy common to both arms; conditional project-skill effect, not pristine machine or isolated single-skill attribution
Trusted fixtures only; generated checks run in network-disabled read-only credential-free Docker
No actual Claude model trials, native plugin-runtime or App effect claim
Fixed synthetic tasks selected before follow-up results; earlier ceiling-effect experiment motivated this exploratory hypothesis; no held-out population inference
Do not change imported skill bodies, source hashes or licenses for this experiment

pre_execution_amendment.reason: Native preflight rejected fastapi bundle missing its required api-contracts bundle; added declared dependency only before any trial/output/model call. Prompts/checkers/skills unchanged.
